T01: Three doctrinal foundations, then five elements of 'personal temple culture'. The turn is the gratitude correction (temples are not 'big or small'). Dense with direct requests, each softened by 'please'; hesitated between temple worship and gratitude over entitlement for units 24-27 and coded both.
T02: Opens with the death of her son and 'something I would not be able to fix'. The umbrella-versus-rock image carries the correction that obedience does not prevent trial. The sculptor story supplies the receiving-help turn; little scripture, heavy personal narrative.
T03: Moves from apostolic witness to every-member witness. Its distinct contribution is pairing 'I know' with 'I love you'. One clear invitation near the end; coded mostly to bearing testimony.
T04: A family loss narrative used in service of valuing prophets rather than of adversity itself, so loss units also carry the prophets code. Long restoration middle section; scripture cited inline in the published text.
T05: States a four-part pattern of deliverance and walks through it under subheadings. Distinctive for normalizing questions ('not sin or weakness') and for 'how and when', not 'if'. Kenzie Brinkerhoff's story anchors honoring covenants.
T06: A single-topic doctrinal talk on the fast: worship, alignment with God's will, then outward to fast offerings. One explicit invitation followed by an apostolic promise. Long paragraphs, so few units.
T07: Addressed first to serving missionaries, then to the rising generation. Merlin Sanchez's story carries lifelong discipleship. Ends by reading D&C 31 as if to the listener; several subgroup-specific invitations.
T08: The only data-driven talk: survey figures and industry revenue. Argument runs harm, opportunity cost, example to the weak (Paul), then the moral case. Two explicit pleas near the end.
T09: The cold-oatmeal story becomes the analogy for forgetting mercies. Distinct codes: remembering God's goodness, redemption by Christ's righteousness, and the 'asterisk'. Hymn stanza kept as one unit.
T10: Two long narratives (the temple encounter with Elder Oaks; the missionary at the airport) around a short doctrinal core tying the sacrament covenant to daily ministering. 'Divine appointments' is the speaker's own term.
T11: An immunity analogy introduces four 'small and simple things'. A list talk: scripture study, prayer, sacrament, covenants, each with a short story or scripture. Two explicit invitations.
T12: A missionary narrative about a poor widow and the mission president's 'no exceptions'. The talk itself adds that obedience does not exempt from trial, so tithing units sit beside trials-not-removed.
T13: Autobiographical conversion narrative reinterpreted by his wife's sentence, 'It was covenants.' The clearest statement of generational covenant reach in the corpus; ends with direct counsel to parents of struggling children.
T14: Identity and unearned love, with a warning against the 'deceitful lie' placed inside the same talk. Baby-picture story is the anchor. Three stated reasons the doctrine matters; no explicit invitation.
T15: Sustained gliding analogy under subheadings: lift, sink, staying in lift. Units 13-14 of the web page are picture captions and were excluded. Directive list near the end is the source of several invitations.
T16: A 100-mile race and a friend who carried the pack. The doctrinal claim is that Christ 'lengthens our stride' rather than shortens the course; also carries God-works-through-people ('sends us a Ted').
T17: Opens with a friend's 'I can't fix this'. Comfort of the Holy Ghost is the organizing code, joined to resurrection perspective through a long quotation from President Oaks. No explicit invitation.
T18: Addressed to those grieving for loved ones who have turned away. Love is defined as 'not stepping back or sanctioning'. Three numbered suggestions hold the invitations; ends with an apostolic promise.
T19: Hymn text ('How Firm a Foundation') frames the talk; the stanza is one unit. Second half thanks members who act as the Lord's means of succor, so it is coded mostly god-works-through-people.
T20: 'Sawubona' (I see you) joins seeing the individual to divine identity and labels. Closes with a three-item list introduced by 'This week, I invite you to'.
T21: Faith and courage as mutually reinforcing; a chain of short examples. Almost every unit carries spiritual courage, which makes it the talk-specific centre of that code. Ends with a promise, not an invitation.
T22: A paperwork mistake becomes the contrast for taking Christ's name 'by covenant'. Service transforms the server (missionaries who changed, not time). Scripture cited inline.
T23: The 'Trespassers will be prosecuted' sign frames come-as-you-are. A ministering visit that ends in a sealing date carries doing one's best. Two explicit invitations.
T24: Integrity and virtue tied to happiness, with a critique of coarse online discourse. David O. McKay's 'act well thy part' story opens. Repentance closes it as part of integrity.
T25: Built on President Oaks's April 2026 invitation. The most operational talk: a list of phrases to retire and a list to use. Many 'let us' sentences, coded as explicit invitations.
T26: Two 'divine helps': the Savior and covenants. Sacrament passages include 'we do not need to be perfect'. Haggai supplies temple-as-priority, a code used nowhere else this conference.
T27: The President of the Church's main address. Short direct imperatives (focus, hold on, keep, protect) interleaved with doctrine; second half on the Book of Mormon's universal reach, ending in two explicit invitations.
T28: Baptism as individual and unifying; unity in Christ carries most units. The sacrament is presented as unifying. Ends with 'come and see, come and help, and come and belong'.
T29: Addressed to young women. A numbered list of seven practices, each a short imperative, so nearly every list unit is an invitation flagged for that audience.
T30: Tithing through a second lens: recognizing 'significant but subtle' blessings. The bulleted list of blessings was kept as separate units, each coded subtle blessings. No explicit invitation to listeners.
T31: The passport parable introduces ordinances as credentials; then a precise explanation of the Holy Spirit of Promise and of what a faithful spouse cannot lose. Doctrinal exposition with no invitation.
T32: A newlywed argument leads to 'contention is not of me'. Three practices appear as section headings in the published text, so only the repentance paragraph carries an explicit 'let us'.
T33: A child's buttoned sleeve and the woman at the well. 'Quick to help and slow to judge' is the speaker's own phrase and the name of the code. Long paragraphs, few units.
T34: Addressed partly to Primary children. Lehi's fruit organizes three 'fruits': identity, the plan of happiness, the Holy Ghost. Ends with 'love, share, and invite' and a promise.
T35: 'Am I good enough to teach?' answered by love for the Master Teacher. Many one-sentence paragraphs, so the unit count is high. Teaching through love carries most of the talk.
T36: Five principles for standing for truth with love, each with a story, including the speaker's own failure. The densest talk for quoted leaders; love-not-condoning is coded from the Holland and Christofferson quotations.
T37: Brief closing remarks: the invitation to study the talks, the Salt Lake Temple open house, a blessing, and testimony.
